Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Session communications

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Bounds and transportRecovery semanticsObserver display names

replay/comms supplies bounded host-ordered chat and positional markers outside simulation. World, action/event schemas and gameplay checkpoints stay unchanged. The Godot adapter uses the existing gameplay connection and recovery router.

Odin
import co "godot:replay/comms"
import rgd "godot:replay/godot"

chat: co.Comms // keep at a stable address beside Session/Room
assert(co.init(&chat))
options := rgd.SESSION_OPTIONS
assert(rgd.session_comms_enable(&options))
// Open Session/Room using options.

// After each Session/Room.frame, including reconnect/fenced frames:
rgd.session_comms_frame(&chat, &session)
co.say(&chat, "found a torch")
co.mark(&chat, 1, {330, 210, 0}) // application-defined nonzero tag
for {
    marker, found := co.poll_marker(&chat)
    if !found {break}
    // Present once; expire using the presentation clock.
}
for {
    receipt, found := co.poll_result(&chat)
    if !found {break}
    // receipt.submission identifies the local submission; value is owned by value.
    // Present failures, and retain/repopulate the original text if desired.
}
// Render chat.lines[:chat.line_count] when chat.history_serial changes.
// co.destroy(&chat) before releasing its containing owner.

The caller's text and marker positions are copied into value payloads. Text is clipped at a UTF-8 rune boundary to 240 bytes. Empty/malformed text and control or line-separator characters fail validation. The UI should render plain text; the Cavecrawl view explicitly disables BBCode. Each line stores the admitted seat, token hash and optional approved display name separately from text. There is no client-supplied speaker field. Display names, permissions and game-specific position checks remain application policy. Pass authority-observed []lobby.Name values to session_comms_frame to stamp names at delivery creation. Existing lines keep their original name after a rename; changing display metadata does not reset connection retry/acknowledgement state.

A client sends one numbered request at a time and waits for its result. Retries repeat the same request identity. The host stamps the speaker from the current admission roster, orders accepted messages, and echoes them to the sender through the same delivery path. Duplicate acknowledgements cannot consume a later request. Observers can chat but cannot create positional markers. Only the authority can call system to publish an unattributed system line.

None from say/mark means queued locally. Drain poll_result for each submission and its copied payload; the authority may reject with Rate_Limited or Capacity. Unread results retain their reserved submission slots, so they cannot be overwritten. last_result / result_serial also summarize the latest outcome. A rejected submission is not silently promoted to a delivery. The default limit is four messages of burst capacity, refilling at two per second for each sender. System lines bypass that per-sender bucket, but still obey queue capacity.

Bounds and transport#

The component retains 64 chat/system lines, eight local submissions, 32 pending marker notifications and 128 outgoing deliveries per connection, for at most 32 connections. Its peer storage is allocated once at initialization. Rendering a smaller window of history is a UI choice. Marker overflow is counted explicitly. A broadcast reserves capacity at every current recipient before committing to the host's history. A slow recipient can therefore cause new submissions to receive Capacity; it cannot silently lose an accepted broadcast from that queue.

Traffic uses a canonical version-2 communications schema envelope, kind 0x434d, current content, room, authority epoch and per-recipient connection generation. Source transport identity comes from the adapter. The receiver validates all of these, the request direction, payload and speaker rules. Checksums detect corruption; they are not cryptographic authentication. The authority is trusted to order and stamp messages.

Comms gets an independent application lane through recovery.link_add_application. It can coexist with the original application lane used by Session assets. The router's total budget and gameplay reserve still apply. Version 2 adds stamped names and does not accept version-1 communications packets. Enable the same service on participating builds; optional service protocols are not negotiated with older builds. Do not attach two consumers to the same route.

The pure configure/frame API accepts an explicitly authenticated roster. The Godot facade derives that roster from live Session connections and checks the current permit before pumping. Applications using the pure API must provide the same admission, authority and clock discipline. No received message grants state ownership, a gameplay action or authority to migrate.

Recovery semantics#

Local scrollback survives a same-room authority change. A successor starts its new epoch's ordering and catches new connections up from the chat lines it actually received. Late joiners receive chat history, not expired marker events. Local history deduplicates using increasing (epoch, sequence) identities; reconnect never appends older catchup lines after newer lines already displayed. Changing room/content clears the local history. Authority epoch regression is rejected.

A same-connection gameplay resync keeps communications active: it replaces the gameplay baseline, not the admitted communications binding. Queued requests, reliable deliveries and their sequence frontier survive that resync. A client still needs a previously accepted world/generation and any required valid permit.

Pending local submissions are retired on fencing or scope/connection replacement, with Scope_Changed and scope_drops explaining the loss. Already received lines remain visible. This is ephemeral session history, not a durable messaging service: a killed host can lose lines that never reached its successor. Fresh process save/resume does not reconstruct chat. Persisting or moderating chat, private/team channels, identity display names and account services need their own explicit policies. Durable gameplay consequences belong in the simulation or a committed service, not in chat callbacks.

Tests cover ordered echo, marker delivery, malformed UTF-8, clipping, spoofed speakers, stale connections, duplicate acknowledgements, rate/capacity limits, bounded late-join history and fencing. Cavecrawl adds real native and browser integration gates alongside its normal gameplay/migration tests.

Observer display names#

An observer can attach a validated display label to a chat submission when its admitted Binding.observer_name_allowed capability is enabled. The sender captures the name with the queued payload, so renaming does not alter retries or historical entries. Empty labels retain the ordinary fallback. Names are bounded UTF-8 single lines under the existing lobby-name validation rules; they are not unique or verified account identities.

The authority always supplies the speaker identity and seat from the admitted binding. A player cannot override its authoritative name through this observer path, and observer markers/system-message claims remain forbidden. A configured authority name still supplies the fallback when a request has no label.

Godot's Session adapter negotiates Features bit 1024 in both directions before allowing these labels. session_comms_frame accepts an optional observer_name separately from the player-seat name array. Old clients keep empty name claims; new clients keep that behavior when an old server does not confirm support. Packet version 2 and its schema are unchanged: this uses the existing Entry.name field. Reconnect and authority replacement clear negotiation until the new handshake.
